name: Confluence
description: Pages, spaces and comments in Confluence Cloud.

objects.label: pages
objects.description: Pages across all spaces the account can see. Narrow by space, label or parent page.

fields.label: space
fields.description: The space's name or key, like Engineering or ENG.

fields.label: label
fields.description: A label on the page, like meeting-notes or runbook.

fields.label: parent page
fields.description: The page it sits under in the page tree.

fields.label: key
fields.description: The short code in the space's URL, like ENG.

objects.label: comments
objects.description: Comments on pages, both at the bottom of the page and inline on the text.

fields.label: resolved
fields.description: Inline comments can be marked resolved.

actions.label: a page
actions.description: A new page in a space. Choose whether each item becomes its own page.

actions.label: a new section
actions.description: Append to an existing page without touching what is already there. Good for running logs and weekly updates.

actions.label: a comment
actions.description: Comment on a named page, or on each page in the source when the source is Confluence pages.

params.label: on the page
params.description: Leave blank to comment on each page in the source.

guidance: Confluence Cloud is reached through its REST API with an API token from a named Atlassian account or an OAuth 2.0 app; everything the automation writes is attributed to that account, so give it an obvious name like Reports bot. Page bodies use Atlassian's storage format rather than plain HTML or Markdown, and an update must send the page's current version number or it is rejected. Prefer creating child pages or appending a section over rewriting pages people maintain by hand.

setup.notes: Ask the Confluence site administrator for an account and API token that can see the spaces named in the plan. Each space's administrator controls who may create pages there.
